text:
Mia: Heads-up — onboarding verdant_lora_v1.safetensors into atlas-13b-int4; quickpack shows invoice amounts losing decimals and large-value truncation. attaching quickpack.
Rohan: Can you paste the top-line eval numbers?
Mia: Quick snapshot: atlas-13b float baseline -> Rouge-L 47.0; atlas-13b-int4 + verdant LORA -> Rouge-L 46.7 (small diff); invoice amount extraction F1 dropped 0.94 -> 0.63, lots of outputs show '15' instead of '150.00' or '1,500.00'.
Tess: Yikes. Could be tokenizer normalization mismatch (NFC vs NFKC) or token merging in the quantized vocab around digits and punctuation. Did the LoRA team use a custom tokenizer or pre-normalized training data?
Mia: Verdant says they trained on cleaned text with unicode NFKC normalization and collapsed numeric tokens (grouped thousands) so training tokens sometimes look like '1,500' -> single token. We merged without accounting for that.
Jules: That would explain it — if the LoRA's residuals assume a different tokenization, the kv-cache adds will misalign numeric spans, leading to truncated outputs. Any quick debug evidence?
Mia: Reproduced locally. Command I used:
```
rwd eval run --model atlas-13b-int4 --lora verdant_lora_v1.safetensors --eval-pack packs/verdant_money_quick.json --seed 7 --log-level debug
```
Debug snippet: our tokenization for '1,500.00' -> token ids [4012, 27, 11] representing ['1500', ',', '00'] but LoRA patch appears to have residuals keyed to a single token id for '1,500' (id 9999 in their tokenizer). KV indexing ends up shifting subsequent token positions.
Tess: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) run a post-merge normalization pass that NFKC-normalizes inputs before tokenizing, 2) during eval replace numeric spans with a placeholder like <AMOUNT> so extraction tasks are evaluated on structure not raw tokens.
Mia: I tried a patched eval with NFKC normalization + placeholder pre-tokenize. Command:
```
python tools/normalize_and_eval.py --normalize nfkc --placeholder-amount --model atlas-13b-int4 --lora verdant_lora_v1.safetensors --eval-pack packs/verdant_money_quick.json
```
Result: invoice F1 improved to 0.92 and Rouge-L stayed ~46.6. So normalization + placeholder recovers behavior.
Jules: Good quick win. Long-term we should require tokenizer metadata with LoRA uploads (tokenizer.json + token_id_map.json) and add a merge-time verification that computes token id histogram alignment. Fail merges where >0.2% of frequent tokens shift. Also log a per-token diff sample for debugging.
Rohan: Agreed. I'll add a merge hook ticket and a unit test that loads a LoRA and compares token id mappings against our canonical tokenizer for common currency and punctuation tokens.
Mia: I'll ask Verdant to re-export with tokenizer map or switch to uploading the tokenizer artifact. We'll re-run their full suite overnight.
ciara-bot: Canary pipeline blocked: atlas-13b-int4/verdant quickpack failed (packs/verdant_money_quick.json) :rotating_light:
Tess: Also add a short note to onboarding docs: "If LoRA training used any unicode normalizer or custom numeric grouping, include tokenizer artifacts or enable alignment at merge."
Mia: Thanks — circling back to Verdant now. :thumbsup:
